_comment: Homestead's own magic balancing. The big temple sends out a priest of its people as soon as it is finished and then every priestSeconds. Small temples turn their people's drink into mana for their player, one unit every templeSeconds (mana per unit below). Each people's priests know its own spell and the common spells; each costs its cost in mana, growing with every cast of it (costIncrease). A spell works on the soldiers within radius of the point it is cast at; that point must be within rangeFactor times the bowmen's range of the priest (data/military.json) and someone it works on must be there (enemy soldiers; Freeze also enemy priests; Haste own soldiers; SummonGoods works anywhere). Priests can be attacked (health).
_rangeComment: rangeFactor: spells are cast from up to this many times the bowmen's range (data/military.json).
_costComment: costIncrease: percent each cast of a spell makes the player's next one of the same spell dearer, rounded up (original: 25 – 20, 25, 32, 40 …; wiki.siedler3.net, Mana & Magie); 0 = constant. The settings (military tab) override it for new games.
_castComment: castSeconds: how long the priest stands casting; the spell takes effect at once when it begins.
_spellsComment: name: shown in the menu. Convert: up to count enemy soldiers change sides (they keep their people, only the color changes). Haste: own soldiers strike factor times as fast for seconds. Freeze: every enemy soldier and priest stands still for seconds (neither walks nor fights). Scatter: up to count enemy soldiers are put on random free points of the map.
_commonSpellsComment: Spells every people knows, after its own. SummonGoods needs no fight: piles (min, max) piles of amount (min, max) goods appear around the target, each of a random group, then a random material of it; extra: further piles per people, each with its chance.
_menuComment: The priests' spell menu per people, top to bottom like the original (icons: spellMenu in data/ui.json). spell: an implemented spell of the people (its own or a common one); placeholder: a spell of the original not made yet – shown with its cost and charge (mana / cost), cannot be cast; names (spells.<id>) and costs are guesses from the icons. Where the Egyptians' Scatter and the Asians' Samurai sword sit is a guess too.
_upgradesComment: Soldier upgrades at a small temple (like the original): first all three soldier types one after the other to level 2 (Feldwebel), only then to level 3 (Hauptmann). Only soldiers trained afterwards get the new level. Mana goes to two accounts: spells spend it, upgrades only ask how much the player has earned in all (they spend nothing). manaEarned: mana earned in all for the player's 1st, 2nd, ... upgrade, whichever type (estimates).
